en.headline: Talent schemes could add 1.2pc to GDP yearly, Lee says
en.dek: The chief executive told a radio programme that more than 300,000 people had arrived under various admission measures, with over half of those reaching the three-year mark willing to stay.
body: Chief Executive John Lee said talent attracted under Hong Kong’s various admission schemes could contribute about 1.2 per cent to the city’s gross domestic product each year.

Speaking on a phone-in radio programme on Friday, Lee said the government had brought in more than 300,000 people through its talent measures, roughly 20 per cent of them from places outside the mainland. He added that more than half of those who had reached the three-year mark were willing to remain in Hong Kong.

Lee said the arrivals were highly qualified and therefore generated meaningful economic output. The remarks came days after he delivered his policy address and unveiled the city’s first five-year plan, which places continued emphasis on attracting and retaining talent.

zh.headline: 李家超：人才計劃每年或為本地生產總值貢獻1.2%
zh.dek: 特首在電台表示，各項人才措施已吸引逾30萬人來港，約兩成來自海外，過半滿三年者有意留港。
body: 行政長官李家超周五在電台電話節目表示，透過各項人才入境措施來港的人才，每年或可為香港本地生產總值貢獻約1.2%。
他說政府已透過人才措施吸引超過30萬人來港，當中約兩成來自內地以外地方。至於已屆滿三年的人才，過半數有意繼續留在香港。
李家超指這些人才質素高，因此能創造可觀的經濟產出。有關言論是在他發表施政報告及公布本港首個五年規劃數日後作出，該規劃繼續強調吸引及挽留人才。
